title: EMT: An OS Framework for New Memory Translation Architectures
problem: Emerging memory translation architectures (beyond traditional page-based virtual memory) lack OS-level support, limiting their adoption and performance optimization in systems.
motivation: OS framework support for novel memory translation mechanisms enables efficient deployment of emerging memory architectures.
method: EMT creates a flexible translation layer in the operating system that maps virtual addresses (the addresses programs use) to physical memory addresses (actual RAM locations). It supports both traditional page tables—fixed-size memory blocks managed by the OS—and alternative translation schemes. By abstracting away the specific translation method, the same OS can work with different architectural approaches without needing separate implementations.
key_novelty: EMT is an operating system framework that supports multiple memory translation architectures (different hardware mechanisms for mapping virtual to physical addresses) instead of being locked into a single translation approach.
contributions: Flexible OS abstraction for diverse memory translation schemes
Backwards compatibility with traditional virtual memory
limitations: Generalization to diverse memory architectures; performance overhead of abstraction layer.
